Jonas / team — quick legal read:

- Subprocessor approval SLA: we're uncomfortable with a hard 7-business-day SLA that constrains our security review cadence. Propose replacing with: "Redwood will notify Customer and use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to subprocessor requests within 10 business days; in emergency cases Redwood will expedite." This preserves operational flexibility but gives the customer expectation.

- Evidence for approval process: we can provide an auditor bundle: subprocessor register export (CSV), ticket timestamps, and an explanatory note on our onboarding flow. I will prepare a redlined paragraph that references the bundle (see attached).

- Export-controls carveout: need specifics on which dataset labels they consider "restricted". Karthik — can your team map MedSyn's sample dataset tags to our retention/access model? If it's strictly EU-hosted processors with standard safeguards, we can handle under our SCCs exhibit; if they require contractual prohibitions on certain transfers, we may need a localized addendum.

I'll draft counter redlines and ask for internal sign-off. If MedSyn insists on the SLA, flag for escalation.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: DPA / SCCs: subprocessor approvals & transfer addendum - MedSyn redlines

Laura / Jonas — quick ops validation:

- The EU-hosted processor list they provided looks to be standard SaaS analytics and logging vendors hosted in EU regions. No blockers from our side for permitting those subprocessors under SCCs.

- Regarding the "restricted dataset" tag: our current data classification has two flags that might align (PII-sensitive, Regulated Health Data). If MedSyn's "restricted" overlaps with Regulated Health Data, we'll need a technical and contractual control (e.g., no export outside EU except with explicit customer opt-in). That would require a localized transfer addendum.

- Evidence: we can export the subprocessor register and provide a time-stamped onboarding record. We can deliver that within 3 business days once legal signs off to share it.

Recommend: Laura, propose the softened SLA language + commit to the auditor bundle. If MedSyn asks for strict export prohibitions for Regulated Health Data, we can offer a short transfer addendum (additional T&Cs) with region-locking options but that will require CS and infra to scope.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Ops, Redwood Inference

Clara — thanks for the redlines and for the patience. Quick summary and next steps from our side: 

1) Subprocessor SLA: Redwood proposes replacing the hard 7-business-day SLA with the following clause: "Redwood will notify Customer and use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to subprocessor requests within 10 business days. In emergency situations Redwood will prioritize and expedite approvals where reasonably practicable." Laura will insert this into the DPA and provide the language in a marked copy by EOD 10/17.

2) Auditor evidence: we can provide a subprocessor register export and onboarding ticket timestamps as an auditor bundle. We'll deliver it to your security contact within 3 business days after you confirm the request.

3) Transfer addendum: Karthik confirms the submitted EU processors are acceptable under our SCCs. If MedSyn defines "restricted" as Regulated Health Data and requires region-locking, we can offer a short transfer addendum that blocks exports outside the EU for the specified categories. That addendum will need a CS/Infra scoped change and could add 2-3 weeks to implementation if region-locking is requested.

4) Timeline: Laura to send redlined DPA by 10/17; Karthik to prepare the auditor bundle export by 10/20; if you want a transfer addendum for region-locking, please flag that by 10/19 so we can scope.

If you'd like to discuss live, I'm available for a 20-minute sync tomorrow at 11:00 CET.
